headline: product-catalog GetProduct failing intermittently on 'Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag' — cascading 500s into cart, recommendations, product pages, and checkout via frontend. Sustained heavy failure 07:56-08:20 UTC, tapering to intermittent bursts since, quiet for last ~6 min. High confidence.
severity_reasoning: Checkout is a revenue-critical path: during the sustained window (07:56-08:20 UTC) the load-generator's own client-side counters show ~47% of /api/checkout calls and 38-47% of /api/products/* and /api/recommendations calls failing with HTTP 500 (e.g. checkout 144 failed vs 162 ok = 47.1%; product 0PUK6V6EV0 105 failed vs 119 ok = 46.9%). A user cannot complete a purchase or view a product roughly half the time during active bursts. Not rated critical because the failure is intermittent/self-recovering rather than a total, unrecovering outage, and traffic volume in this environment is synthetic.
hypothesis: The product-catalog service is deliberately rejecting a subset of GetProduct RPCs via its 'Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag' (flagd flag likely productCatalogFailure, description: 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product'), returning gRPC INTERNAL (code 13). Because nearly every frontend page (product detail, cart, recommendations, checkout) calls GetProduct to hydrate product data, this single upstream failure cascades into 500s across all of those user-facing routes. The failure is bursty (started sustained ~07:56, eased ~08:20-08:23, then intermittent bursts through ~08:50, quiet since ~08:53), consistent with a flag being probabilistically evaluated or cycled by the demo's fault scenario rather than a hard-down dependency.
disconfirming_checks: Checked gRPC status codes for every backend service via rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count in Mimir over the last 15m: only 'ad' showed a non-zero status code label present (status 14, but increase()=0 in-window) — no other service showed backend gRPC errors, so this is not a broad multi-service outage, it isolates to product-catalog.

Checked Loki ERROR-level logs for product-catalog, recommendation, checkout, frontend-proxy: all returned 0 streams — the failure is visible in trace spans/status, not in application log lines, so log-only triage would have missed this entirely; corroborated via Tempo trace search instead.

Verified the 500s are not client-side/load-generator artifacts by pulling full traces (e.g. traceid 90620f08e78535ebd0cab38f15a5fd37) end-to-end: frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog, with product-catalog's own span carrying status=error and message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' — the error originates inside product-catalog, not at the proxy or frontend layer.

Considered whether this is normal baseline noise: baseline unrelated endpoints (api/data?contextKeys=accessories/binoculars, which don't call product-catalog) show only 1.5-1.8% failure in the same window, so the 38-47% failure rate on product/cart/recommendations/checkout is specific to this dependency, not general system noise.

Checked whether it has already fully resolved: increase() of product-catalog error spans in 3-minute buckets over the last hour shows sustained 145-520 errors/3min from 07:56-08:20, dropping to 0 at 08:23-08:29, then residual bursts (88.5, 316.5, 147) through 08:50, then 0 at 08:53 and 08:56 — two clean buckets, but prior gaps of similar length (08:23-08:32, 08:41-08:47) also went quiet before another burst, so I'm not calling this resolved yet; treating it as tapering/intermittent, not closed.

Checked flagd's /status/<flag> endpoint for all 15 known flags: all report only defaultVariant='off', which is static default metadata, not live runtime state — flagd here doesn't expose an authoritative 'currently active' read, so I could not directly confirm the flag's live value and instead relied on the product-catalog span's own error message as the evidence of cause.

evidence.raw: http://frontend-proxy:8080/api/products/0PUK6V6EV0 500 105 vs 200 119 (46.9% failed); http://frontend-proxy:8080/api/checkout 500 144 vs 200 162 (47.1% failed); http://frontend-proxy:8080/api/recommendations?productIds=0PUK6V6EV0 500 26 vs 200 23 (comparable magnitude across all 10 product IDs, 38-47% failure each)
